intro: Step into the rock and meet the gods. You are at Yazılıkaya, a sanctuary in Çorum province from the 13th century BC. This was the open-air sanctuary of Hattusa: along the walls of two rock chambers, a procession of more than sixty gods and goddesses is carved in relief.
history: These rock clefts, a kilometre and a half north-east of Hattusa, formed the largest open-air sanctuary of the Hittite empire. On the walls of Chamber A, two processions of gods walk towards each other and meet in the middle, at the chief god and goddess. Chamber B is dedicated to king Tudhaliya IV. The reliefs were carved in the thirteenth century BC: the Hittite roll of gods, set into stone.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the procession in Chamber A, then Chamber B with the relief of Tudhaliya IV, and look for the sword god Nergal.
facts: Did you know? Most of the gods in the procession have their names written beside their heads in Luwian hieroglyphs, and it was those inscriptions that made the Hittite pantheon legible. More than sixty gods and goddesses walk in relief along the walls of these two rock chambers: the Hittite pantheon, set into stone.
outro: This brings our journey through Yazılıkaya to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These gods have walked here for centuries; let them keep walking for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
